disagreements.post_excerpt: Booking done for plumber in the time slot of 9 to 9.30 AM, plumber came at 12.30 PM after repeated calls. Basin mixure was installed well within 15 minute . But
disagreements.human_note:
. Executive Summary
The customer experienced a 3-hour arrival delay requiring repeated follow-ups, and although the physical installation was done quickly (under 15 mins), they walked away with a strong perception of being overcharged due to rigid, flat-rate catalog pricing that fails to differentiate between a quick 15-minute job and a complex, time-intensive installation.


2. Breakdown of Core Issues
Issue 1: Severe Punctuality & Coordination Friction (SLA Breach)
What happened: Booked for 9:00 AM – 9:30 AM; technician arrived at 12:30 PM (a 3-hour delay).
Customer effort: The customer had to make repeated follow-up calls to get the professional to show up, leading to wasted time and high coordination anxiety.
Issue 2: Perceived Price–Effort Mismatch (Catalog Granularity Problem)
What happened: Urban Company charges the exact same flat rate for both:
Countertop basin mixer (quick, simple fitting — completed in under 15 minutes).
Wall-mounted sink mixer (complex, requires drilling/in-wall pipe alignment — takes much longer).
Customer grievance: The customer felt the listed price was fair for a difficult wall-mounted job, but felt overcharged for a simple 15-minute countertop installation.


3. Why This Drives Churn (The 90-Day Repeat Booking Impact)
"Never Again for Small Jobs" Mental Model: Even though the physical work was satisfactory, the customer felt the cost-per-minute was unreasonable. Next time they need a quick 10–15 minute fix (tap change, washer replacement), they will likely hire a local neighborhood plumber (who charges ₹100–₹200) instead of paying UC's flat rate.
Erosion of the "Convenience Premium": Customers pay Urban Company a premium over local unorganized labor specifically for punctuality and hassle-free scheduling. When a professional is 3 hours late and requires chasing, the platform loses its primary justification for charging higher rates.
